name: Cai Rang floating market
kicker: Wholesale boats and cây bẹo poles at dawn
summary: Ride a small boat among the wholesale boats while the light is still low. Sellers hang fruit or vegetables on a cây bẹo pole so a buyer can see the goods. The department lists 60 minutes at the market. Publishers print different clocks, and every figure stays in the hours.
getThere: About 30 minutes by boat from Ninh Kiều
heroCaption: Trading boats at Cái Răng, with pineapples on the water

notice.title: A late bus misses the wholesale boats
notice.body: Vietnam Tourism says be on the water by 5:00 or 5:30, leaving Ninh Kiều around 5:00. A same-morning ride from Ho Chi Minh City arrives after that.

body: The boats are wholesale, not a souvenir stall. Sellers hang a sample on a long pole, the cây bẹo, so a buyer can see the goods without a shout over the engines. The Can Tho Portal of 4 January 2016 also describes calling and bargaining. Breakfast boats sell hủ tiếu, bún riêu, and coffee. Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch thành phố Cần Thơ says the market’s trading culture was put on the national intangible-heritage list in 2016.

The department listing puts the market in phường Cái Răng and lists 60 minutes at the spot. The ride from Ninh Kiều is about 30 minutes on that listing and on Vietnam Tourism’s four-day piece. The national dining page says six kilometres. A department reprint of 21 December 2019 says 6 km by road from the centre, or 30 minutes by water, and that the market thins around 8:00–9:00. The 2016 portal says a few kilometers. Vietnam Tourism’s place page also prints “46 Hai Bà Trưng, Ninh Kiều.” Hai Bà Trưng is the quay street in Ninh Kiều. Do not treat that number as the mooring.

Flood months from September to November are the season Vietnam Tourism’s place page ties to this boat. The accounts read for the city do not give the market a closed season. Arrive before the boats pack up. The clocks in the hours do not agree, so none of them is dropped.

figures.caption: Cabbages and a trader on a Cái Răng boat
figures.alt: A trader beside a pile of cabbages on a boat at the Cai Rang floating market

gettingThere: Leave from Bến Ninh Kiều. The department listing says about 30 minutes by boat, and that you can also leave from piers closer to the market. Those pier names were not printed. Check on arrival. By road, the dining page and the 21 December 2019 department reprint say 6 km from the centre. The Can Tho Portal of 4 January 2016 says a few kilometers.

legs.heading: From Ninh Kiều
legs.body: Small boat, about 30 minutes, on the department listing and on Vietnam Tourism’s four-day piece. Rise at 5:00 if you are using that piece’s clock. Boat hire on the listing is đang cập nhật. The department advice page prints 300,000–700,000 VND a boat, depending on the number of guests.

legs.heading: From Ho Chi Minh City
legs.body: Sleep in Can Tho the night before. Vietnam Tourism prints about 165 km. Vietnamese Wikipedia prints 155 km between centres. The expressway reports print 120 km of expressway and about 2 hours or hơn 2 giờ. A departure that same morning misses the wholesale boats.

hours: Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch thành phố Cần Thơ lists clock fields from 4:00 to 12:00, and says the useful visit is 5:00–7:00. The 12:00 close reads as a full-day form, not a counted market end. Vietnam Tourism’s place page says 4:30–8:00. Vietnam Tourism’s floating-flavour page says be on the water by 5:00 or 5:30, and that vendors pack up by 8:00. Vietnam Tourism’s four-day piece says early morning to midday, and to rise at 5:00. Vietnam Tourism’s towns page says the market starts around 5:00 and to be on a boat by 6:00. The Can Tho Portal of 4 January 2016 says 5:00–9:00. Another Can Tho Portal page says the market opens from 5:00 and is busiest from 6:00 to 9:00. The city’s top-7 page says 4:30–6:30. A Can Tho Portal page that credits Tourismcantho.vn says 4:30–8:00. The department advice page says 5:00–9:00. A department reprint of 21 December 2019 says the market thins around 8:00–9:00.
closed: No weekly closing day is printed. Check on arrival.
admissionNote: The department listing prints đang cập nhật for a ticket and does not print a boat fare. The department advice page prints 300,000–700,000 VND a boat, depending on the number of guests. Vietnam Tourism’s place page does not print a fare. Check on arrival.
